     return pluralize(underscore(word))
 
 
+def _acronyms(word: str) -> typing.List[typing.Optional[str]]:
+    """
+    Return the words that :func:`titleize` makes of ``word``, in order: each
+    one as it was written if it is in all caps, or ``None`` if it is not.
+    """
+    # Split the words like underscore() does, but without lowercasing them.
+    split = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    split = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', split)
+    acronyms: typing.List[typing.Optional[str]] = []
+    # Words can be joined by apostrophes, as in "NASA's" or "DON'T". A part
+    # after an apostrophe only counts if the part before it does, so that
+    # "Rock'N'Roll" still becomes "Rock'n'roll".
+    for joined in re.findall(r"[^\W_]+(?:'[^\W_]+)*", split):
+        is_acronym = True
+        for part in joined.split("'"):
+            is_acronym = is_acronym and part.isupper()
+            acronyms.append(part if is_acronym else None)
+    return acronyms
+
+
 def titleize(word: str) -> str:

     Capitalize all the words and replace some characters in the string to
@@ -371,12 +391,32 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
 
+    Words in all caps, such as the acronyms ``NASA`` and ``HTTP``, are kept as
+    they are, unless the whole string is in uppercase::
+
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
+
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        return title
+    # Put the acronyms back. With a capturing group, re.split() puts the words
+    # at the odd indexes.
+    pieces = re.split(r"([^\W_]+)", title)
+    for index, acronym in zip(range(1, len(pieces), 2), _acronyms(word)):
+        # Comparing the letters guards against the rare characters whose
+        # lowercase form is longer, like the Turkish dotted I, which would
+        # shift the words.
+        if acronym and acronym.lower() == pieces[index].lower():
+            pieces[index] = acronym
+    return ''.join(pieces)
